title: Public evidence and assessment boundary
outcomes: Every public surface renders one versioned country-aware evidence and assessment truth.
Every enabled source enters through a rights-approved, provenance-complete, privacy-minimized projection.
Uncertainty, source failure, spoofing risk, and absence of evidence remain explicit and actionable.

in: Phone-number normalization, source evidence, assessment, campaign, and transparency contracts.
Rights-approved source manifests, ingestion adapters, generated read models, and freshness controls.
Read-only CLI, stdio MCP, hosted MCP, HTTP, web, and Vercel delivery boundaries.
Public safety language, source coverage, provenance, and operational failure semantics.
out: Public first-party report collection and moderation.
Persistent private watches, organisation submissions, and outbound notifications.
Selection of a future mutable store, queue, analytics platform, identity provider, or licensed reputation vendor.
Subscriber, caller, current-provider, reachability, location, guilt, or safety attribution.
boundaries: Untrusted phone input and explicit region context enter the normalization boundary.
External regulator, numbering, and complaint data enter only through reviewed source manifests and minimization builders.
Generated catalogues expose bounded evidence observations without raw source rows, holder data, plaintext inventories, or secrets.
The deterministic domain result crosses into transport and presentation adapters without a second verdict path.
Deployment secrets cross only into build and read-model authentication; they never reach clients, logs, fixtures, or Git.

concerns: Traceable evidence, limitations, and a safe next action.
No unsupported identity or safety claim.
decision_rights: Expect stable versioned public contracts and correction-aware evidence.

concerns: Replaceable adapters and deterministic local gates.
Operationally supportable source and deployment boundaries.
decision_rights: Approve reversible implementation choices within accepted architecture decisions.
Require a new decision when a material boundary or quality attribute changes.

concerns: Data rights, privacy, public safety, and hard-to-reverse commitments.
Named accountability for exceptions and residual risk.
decision_rights: Approve new personal-data processing, public mutation, identity claims, providers, and foundational trust-boundary changes.
Grant or reject time-bounded architecture waivers and risk acceptance.

concerns: Accurate provenance, permitted fields, correction, and takedown behavior.
decision_rights: Define source access and reuse terms that CallerSignal must honor.

constraints: A displayed number is evidence context and never proof of caller, subscriber, provider, reachability, guilt, or safety.
National input requires an explicit origin region; E.164 is the canonical internal number representation.
Lookup demand, numbering facts, identity claims, reports, source observations, and assessments remain separate.
Only documented official, public-domain, explicitly licensed, or approved first-party moderated evidence may affect reputation.
One unverified source cannot produce elevated_signals or official_warning, regardless of observation count.
Source failure, staleness, conflict, or unsupported coverage fails closed to a typed evidence gap.
CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web consume the shared domain contracts and may not calculate independent verdicts.
Raw complaints, plaintext or keyed number inventories, source-holder fields, lookup histories, credentials, and generated databases are excluded from Git and public responses.
Public mutation remains disabled until privacy, identity, consent, moderation, retention, correction, deletion, appeal, rate, and provider controls have executable proof.

quality_attributes.scenario: A canonical lookup, campaign, methodology, or coverage result is exposed through multiple public interfaces.
quality_attributes.measure: Contract or semantic mismatches across CLI, stdio MCP, hosted MCP, HTTP, and web in the canonical gate.

quality_attributes.scenario: A source is proposed or activated for numbering or reputation evidence.
quality_attributes.measure: Enabled sources missing validated authority, reuse basis, permitted fields, provenance, freshness, outage, correction, or takedown controls.

quality_attributes.scenario: Repository state, build artifacts, public responses, screenshots, or release evidence are produced.
quality_attributes.measure: Committed or publicly exposed secrets, raw complaint rows, holder data, personal lookup history, or plaintext/keyed number inventories.

quality_attributes.scenario: Input is ambiguous or invalid, a source is unavailable, stale, conflicting, unsupported, or returns no match.
quality_attributes.measure: Cases that produce a safety, identity, elevated, or official-warning claim without the required eligible evidence and typed residual uncertainty.

quality_attributes.scenario: A new developer or agent clones the repository and validates the public read-only product.
quality_attributes.measure: Required repository, workflow, schema, documentation, asset, privacy, or test gates that cannot be run from documented prerequisites.

risks: Caller ID spoofing or number portability can make displayed-number evidence look like caller identity.
External source formats, semantics, licences, availability, or correction paths can change without notice.
Dynamic build-time catalogues can drift from committed transparency expectations if generation and parity gates diverge.
A transport or UI can accidentally create a second verdict path or overstate source confidence as safety probability.
Secrets, raw source rows, personal reports, or lookup histories can leak through generated artifacts, logs, screenshots, or workflow evidence.
Pressure for coverage can bypass source rights, minimization, moderation, or independent-corroboration controls.
open_questions: Which explicitly licensed caller-reputation provider, if any, should become the next independent source?
Which identity, storage, queue, and notification architecture should govern future private watches and verified organisation submissions?
Which named human roles will approve future foundational trust-boundary changes and time-bounded risk waivers?
